claim: In a population-based study of Missouri and Los Angeles County, the estimated mean annual incidence of NAION among people aged 50 years or older was 2.30 per 100,000.
title: Incidence of nonarteritic and arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. Population-based study in the state of Missouri and Los Angeles County, California.
quote: the estimated mean annual incidence rates per 100,000 population were 2.30 for nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy

claim: White individuals appeared to be at significantly higher risk of NAION than Black or Hispanic individuals in that population-based study.
title: Incidence of nonarteritic and arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. Population-based study in the state of Missouri and Los Angeles County, California.
quote: White individuals appear to be at significantly higher risk of developing nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy than black or Hispanic individuals

claim: In Olmsted County, Minnesota (1981-1990), the crude annual incidence of acute NAION was 10.3 per 100,000, with a median age at diagnosis of 72 years.
title: Incidence of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: The crude annual incidence rate was 10.3 per 100,000 individuals (95% confidence interval [CI] = 5.1 to 18.4).

claim: NAION is described as the most common acute optic nerve disease of adults over age 50 years.
title: Incidence of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy is the most common acute optic nerve disease of adults over age 50 years.

claim: A Rochester Epidemiology Project re-examination (1990-2016) estimated NAION incidence at 10.19 per 100,000 among people aged 50 years or older, stable over four decades.
title: Reexamining the Incidence of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: A Rochester Epidemiology Project Study.
quote: The incidence was 7.73 (CI: 6.24-9.22) in patients aged 40 years or older and 10.19 (CI: 8.15-12.23) in patients aged 50 years or older.

claim: In the same population-based cohort, 21.2% of patients developed NAION in the fellow eye, with a median inter-eye interval of 1.39 years.
title: Reexamining the Incidence of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: A Rochester Epidemiology Project Study.
quote: Twenty-two patients (21.2%) suffered NAION in the fellow eye; the median interval between involvement of the first and second eyes was 1.39 years.

claim: Hypertension, diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea and hyperlipidemia were all more prevalent in incident NAION than in age-matched controls.
title: Reexamining the Incidence of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: A Rochester Epidemiology Project Study.
quote: hypertension (79.8%), diabetes mellitus (39.4%), obstructive sleep apnea (23.1%), and hyperlipidemia (74.0%), which were all statistically higher than age-matched controls

claim: In 386 untreated NAION eyes, about half presented with near-normal visual acuity, so normal acuity does not exclude NAION.
title: Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy: natural history of visual outcome.
quote: About half of the eyes with NAION presented with almost normal visual acuity (20/15 to 20/30) at the initial visit.

claim: In untreated NAION, eyes seen within 2 weeks with acuity of 20/70 or worse improved in 41% at 6 months, with changes occurring mainly within the first 6 months.
title: Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy: natural history of visual outcome.
quote: Visual acuity and visual fields showed improvement or further deterioration mainly up to 6 months, with no significant change after that.

claim: In the IONDT follow-up study, new NAION in the fellow eye occurred in 14.7% of at-risk patients over a median 5.1 years.
title: The fellow eye in NAION: report from the ischemic optic neuropathy decompression trial follow-up study.
quote: New NAION in the fellow eye occurred in 14.7% (48/326) of patients at risk during a median follow up of 5.1 years.

claim: Diabetes and poor baseline study-eye acuity, but not age, sex, smoking or aspirin use, were associated with fellow-eye NAION in the IONDT cohort.
title: The fellow eye in NAION: report from the ischemic optic neuropathy decompression trial follow-up study.
quote: A history of diabetes and baseline visual acuity of 20/200 or worse in the study eye, but not age, sex, aspirin use, or smoking were significantly associated with new NAION in the fellow eye.

claim: Among 420 IONDT-eligible patients, mean age at onset was 66 years, 47% reported hypertension and 24% diabetes.
title: Characteristics of patients with nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy eligible for the Ischemic Optic Neuropathy Decompression Trial.
quote: The mean +/- SD age at onset was 66.0 +/- 8.7 years. Hypertension was reported in 47% of the patients in the IONDT, and 24% of the patients had diabetes mellitus.

claim: In the IONDT cohort, 42% of patients recalled onset of visual symptoms within 2 hours of awakening.
title: Characteristics of patients with nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy eligible for the Ischemic Optic Neuropathy Decompression Trial.
quote: Forty-two percent of the patients recalled the onset of visual symptoms to be within 2 hours of awakening.

claim: NAION is characterized by abrupt, painless vision loss with unilateral optic disc edema, typically in patients over 50 with small optic discs and vasculopathic risk factors.
title: Non-Arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy (NA-AION): A Comprehensive Overview.
quote: Unilateral optic disc edema and abrupt, painless vision loss are its defining features.

claim: No effective medical or surgical therapy or prophylactic measure for NAION currently exists.
title: Non-Arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy (NA-AION): A Comprehensive Overview.
quote: no available effective medical or surgical therapy or prophylactic measure for NA-AION currently exists

claim: There are no widely accepted evidence-based treatments for NAION, and advice to reduce sequential-eye risk has only theoretical bases.
title: The enigma of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy: an update for the comprehensive ophthalmologist.
quote: There are currently no widely accepted, evidence-based treatments for NAION.

claim: In a cohort of 113 unilateral NAION patients, diabetes (HR 3.06) and more severe initial field damage predicted fellow-eye involvement.
title: Risk Factors for Fellow Eye Involvement in Patients with Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy.
quote: Diabetes (HR = 3.06, 95% CI: 1.50, 6.26, p = 0.002) and increased VF damage

claim: Recurrence of NAION in the same eye was uncommon (6.4%) in a cohort of 594 patients and was associated with nocturnal diastolic hypotension.
title: Ipsilateral recurrence of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: Recurrence of NA-AION in the same eye is uncommon (6.4%). Our study indicates that nocturnal diastolic arterial hypotension may be a risk factor

claim: In 86 patients with bilateral sequential NAION, visual function in fellow eyes showed a fair-to-moderate, statistically significant correlation.
title: Bilateral sequential nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy: a comparison of visual outcomes in fellow eyes using quantitative analysis of goldmann visual fields.
quote: Visual function between fellow eyes showed a fair to moderate correlation that was statistically significant.

claim: In 406 NAION patients, arterial hypertension and diabetes were significantly more prevalent than in the general population across age groups, and NAION was described as multifactorial with predisposing and precipitating factors.
title: Systemic diseases associated with nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy is a multifactorial disease in which some systemic diseases may act as predisposing factors and others as precipitating factors.

claim: Fellow eyes of NAION patients more often had no cup and less often had large cups than arteritic AION or normal eyes, implicating a small, crowded disc in pathogenesis.
title: Anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. IX. Cup-to-disc ratio and its role in pathogenesis.
quote: The number of discs with no cup was significantly greater (P less than 0.001) and the number of discs with a large cup was significantly fewer (P less than 0.001) in the n-AION group

claim: Discs without a physiologic cup were more frequent than expected in both affected and fellow eyes of patients with acute NAION.
title: Optic disc structure in anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: The number of discs (both involved and fellow) without a physiologic cup was significantly greater than would be expected from normal population studies.

claim: In the 729-participant Quark207 trial cohort, a small fellow-eye cup-to-disc ratio was the most prevalent risk factor, whereas cardiovascular risk factors were not typically more prevalent than in the general population.
title: Ophthalmic and Systemic Factors of Acute Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy in the Quark207 Treatment Trial.
quote: Having a small cup-to-disc ratio in the fellow eye was the most prevalent risk factor across all demographics.

claim: In a multicenter study of NAION patients aged 50 or younger, most had optic disc drusen, suggesting drusen may be an independent risk factor in younger patients.
title: Young Adults With Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: A Multicenter Optic Disc Drusen Study.
quote: Most of these young NA-AION patients had ODD. This indicates that ODD may be an independent risk factor for the development of NA-AION, at least in younger patients.

claim: Patients with drusen-associated AION more often lacked vascular risk factors than similarly aged NAION patients without drusen.
title: Optic Disc Drusen Associated Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: Prevalence of Comorbidities and Vascular Risk Factors.
quote: the ODD-AION patients more often had no vascular risk factors as compared to NA-AION patients

claim: A meta-analysis of 49 studies found male sex, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, coronary heart disease and sleep apnea (RR 3.28) significantly associated with NAION.
title: Risk Factors for Non-arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: A Large Scale Meta-Analysis.
quote: sleep apnea (RR = 3.28, 95% CI: 2.08-5.17, P < 0.00001), factor V Leiden heterozygous (RR = 2.21, 95% CI: 1.19-4.09, P = 0.01)

claim: In a US managed-care cohort of 1.38 million enrollees, hypertension (HR 1.62) and hypercoagulable states (HR 2.46) were associated with incident NAION, while uncomplicated diabetes was not.
title: Demographic, Systemic, and Ocular Factors Associated with Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy.
quote: Systemic diseases associated with NAION included hypertension (HR = 1.62; 95% CI: 1.26-2.07) and hypercoagulable states (HR = 2.46; 95% CI: 1.51-4.00).

claim: In the same cohort, female sex was associated with a lower hazard of NAION and retinal vein occlusion with a higher hazard.
title: Demographic, Systemic, and Ocular Factors Associated with Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy.
quote: Female subjects had a 36% decreased hazard of developing NAION (HR = 0.64; 95% CI: 0.55-0.74) compared with male subjects.

claim: In a case-control study, diabetes was a significant NAION risk factor (OR 2.7-5.0) but its low attributable risk implied other factors are important.
title: Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. A case-control study of potential risk factors.
quote: The low attributable risk estimation suggests that factors other than diabetes are important in the development of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy

claim: In a small polysomnography study, 71% of NAION patients had sleep apnea syndrome versus 18% of matched controls.
title: Association between sleep apnea syndrome and nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: Twelve (71%) of 17 patients with NAION had SAS.

claim: A meta-analysis of five studies estimated a pooled OR of 6.18 for NAION among people with obstructive sleep apnea versus controls.
title: The Association Between Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
quote: The pooled OR of developing NAION in the subjects with OSA was 6.18 (95% CI, 2.00-19.11) versus non-OSA controls.

claim: Ambulatory monitoring in 166 patients suggested nocturnal hypotension may reduce optic nerve head blood flow below a critical level and act as a final insult in AION.
title: Nocturnal arterial hypotension and its role in optic nerve head and ocular ischemic disorders.
quote: nocturnal hypotension may be the final insult in a multifactorial situation

claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis did not find PDE-5 inhibitor use associated with definite NAION (OR 1.16; 95% CI 0.89-1.52), although case reports exist.
title: Risk of nonarteritic ischaemic optic neuropathy with phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
quote: Treatment with phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors is not associated with an increased risk of definitive nonarteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy [odds ratio (OR) 1.16

claim: A review of PDE-5 inhibitors and NAION cited one case-crossover study reporting a 2-fold increase in NAION risk after ingestion.
title: The Relationship Between Phosphodiesterase-5 Inhibitors and Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy.
quote: One case-crossover study demonstrated a 2-fold increase in risk of NAION after ingestion of PDE5I.

claim: A causal link between amiodarone and optic neuropathy has never been firmly established and remains controversial.
title: Amiodarone and optic neuropathy: the heart of the matter.
quote: Although a subject of intense controversy, a causal link between amiodarone and optic neuropathy has never been firmly established.

claim: Thirty-six reports of AION with interferon alfa (67% bilateral, 3 positive rechallenges) supported a 'possible' WHO-category association.
title: Interferon alfa-associated anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: Interferon alfa's association with AION can be classified as "possible" using the World Health Organization classification system.

claim: In 624 NAION patients, the prevalence of smoking did not differ from matched US population rates, indicating no association with smoking.
title: Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy and tobacco smoking.
quote: Our study showed no association between NA-AION and tobacco smoking.

claim: In a case-control study, no genetic or acquired thrombophilic marker was a significant NAION risk factor, whereas ischemic heart disease, hypercholesterolemia and diabetes were.
title: Analysis of prothrombotic and vascular risk factors in patients with nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: None of the thrombophilic markers (genetic and acquired) constituted a significant risk factor for NAION.

claim: A small case-control study (37 cases) found elevated Lp(a), diabetes and factor V Leiden associated with NAION but noted data were insufficient to justify anticoagulant/antiplatelet prophylaxis.
title: Trombophilic screening for nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: Further data are needed, however, to justify the suggested use of secondary prophylaxis using anticoagulant/antiplatelet therapy.

claim: A meta-analysis found a 4.6-fold higher hazard of NAION within 1 year of cataract surgery, though absolute risk remained low (about 1 in 1,000-3,100 surgeries).
title: Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy After Cataract Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
quote: Pooling of 63,823 cataract surgeries and 161,643 controls showed a hazard ratio of 4.6 (95% CI 2.7-7.8) of psNAION within 1 year of surgery.

claim: In Olmsted County, AION incidence was higher within 1 year of cataract surgery (38.9 vs 6.5 per 100,000) but not within 2 months.
title: A Population-Based Study of Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy Following Cataract Surgery.
quote: The incidence of AION is increased in the first year after cataract surgery, but not in the early (i.e., 2 months) postoperative period.

claim: Proposed risk factors for perioperative ischemic optic neuropathy include prolonged prone positioning, blood loss, hypotension, anemia and vasoconstrictors; AION predominates after cardiac surgery.
title: Perioperative visual loss after nonocular surgeries.
quote: excessive blood loss, hypotension, anemia, hypoxia, excessive fluid replacement, use of vasoconstricting agents, elevated venous pressure

claim: Reported cases of AION in chronic dialysis patients commonly shared hypotension and anemia as risk factors.
title: Anterior ischemic optic neuropathy and dialysis: role of hypotension and anemia.
quote: most cases of AION occurring in chronic uremic patients on dialysis have some common features, including hypotension above all and anemia as common risk factors

claim: NAION is attributed to infarction of the laminar/retrolaminar optic nerve head supplied by the short posterior ciliary arteries, with nocturnal hypotension, impaired autoregulation, vasculopathic occlusion and venous insufficiency implicated.
title: Non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy: a review and update.
quote: Factors that have been implicated include nocturnal hypotension, impaired autoregulation of the microvascular supply, vasculopathic occlusion, and venous insufficiency.

claim: These factors are thought to produce axonal edema and a compartment syndrome in a structurally crowded disc, leading to retinal ganglion cell loss.
title: Non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy: a review and update.
quote: These factors are thought to result in axonal oedema causing a compartment syndrome in a structurally crowded optic disc

claim: Crowded discs are predisposed, infarcts are mainly laminar/retrolaminar, and vasculopathy within or distal to paraoptic branches of the posterior ciliary circulation with impaired autoregulation is proposed.
title: Pathogenesis of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: lack of consistent choroidal flow impairment and the retrolaminar location of infarcts suggest vasculopathy within or distal to the paraoptic branches

claim: Diabetes is described as the most consistently identified vasculopathic risk factor for NAION.
title: Pathogenesis of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: diabetes is the most consistently identified vasculopathic risk factor

claim: Three-dimensional reconstruction of a NAION infarct did not match a single vascular territory and was considered more consistent with a compartment syndrome.
title: The morphology of an infarct in nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: The morphology of this NAION infarct is not consistent with disease of large or small vessels and, more likely, represents a form of compartment syndrome

claim: Hayreh argued vascular insufficiency of the optic nerve head underlies AION, while noting conflicting claims about optic nerve head blood supply and its measurement.
title: The blood supply of the optic nerve head and the evaluation of it - myth and reality.
quote: there is vascular insufficiency in the optic nerve head (ONH) in both anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (AION) and glaucomatous optic neuropathy

claim: Beck and colleagues proposed that small disc size contributes through a compressive effect at the lamina cribrosa on ischemic axons.
title: Anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. IX. Cup-to-disc ratio and its role in pathogenesis.
quote: The size of the optic disc also plays a role, probably through a compressive effect at the level of the lamina cribrosa on axons subjected to ischemia.

claim: A rodent photoembolic model (rAION) reproduces electrophysiological and histological changes similar to clinical AION.
title: Functional and cellular responses in a novel rodent model of anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: rAION rapidly results in electrophysiological and histologic changes similar to clinical AION

claim: A primate photoembolic NAION model produced disc edema followed by RGC-layer loss and prolonged optic nerve inflammation.
title: A primate model of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: pNAION resembles human NAION in many respects, with optic disc edema followed by loss of cells in the retinal ganglion cell (RGC) layer

claim: Much of NAION pathophysiology remains unknown; rodent and primate models provide a platform for mechanistic and treatment studies.
title: Non-Arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy (NAION): A Review and Update on Animal Models.
quote: much remains unknown about its pathophysiology and there is no proven treatment

claim: The IONDT found optic nerve decompression surgery was not effective and possibly harmful (23.9% vs 12.4% lost >=3 lines at 6 months) and should be abandoned.
title: Optic nerve decompression surgery for nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) is not effective and may be harmful. The Ischemic Optic Neuropathy Decompression Trial Research Group.
quote: Results from the IONDT indicate that optic nerve decompression surgery for NAION is not effective, may be harmful, and should be abandoned.

claim: In the IONDT, 42.7% of the careful follow-up group improved by >=3 lines at 6 months, indicating better spontaneous improvement than previously reported.
title: Optic nerve decompression surgery for nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) is not effective and may be harmful. The Ischemic Optic Neuropathy Decompression Trial Research Group.
quote: The spontaneous improvement rate is better than previously reported.

claim: At 24 months the IONDT confirmed no benefit of decompression surgery over careful follow-up.
title: Ischemic Optic Neuropathy Decompression Trial: twenty-four-month update.
quote: confirms that there is no benefit of ONDS compared with careful follow-up in patients with nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy

claim: A Cochrane review identified only one randomized surgical trial (IONDT) and found no evidence of benefit; no medical therapy has been proven effective.
title: Surgery for nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: Its etiology is unknown and no medical therapy has been proven effective in treating this condition.

claim: In a nonrandomized cohort of 613 patients who self-selected therapy, systemic corticosteroids were associated with higher rates of acuity improvement (69.8% vs 40.5%).
title: Non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy: role of systemic corticosteroid therapy.
quote: there was visual acuity improvement in 69.8% (95% confidence interval (CI): 57.3%, 79.9%) in the treated group, compared to 40.5%

claim: A 38-patient randomized trial found oral steroids did not significantly improve visual acuity at 6 months in nondiabetic NAION.
title: Steroids versus No Steroids in Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
quote: Oral steroids in acute NAAION did not improve the visual acuity significantly at 6 months.

claim: A meta-analysis of eight studies found steroids did not significantly improve visual acuity in NAION.
title: Steroids in the treatment of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy: A PRISMA-compliant meta-analysis.
quote: steroids did not significantly improve visual acuity (WMD = -0.02 [95% CI: -0.10 to 0.06]

claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 32 studies did not identify any effective NAION treatment.
journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
title: Efficacy of Treatments in Nonarteritic Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
quote: Our systematic review did not reveal any effective treatment.

claim: In a retrospective cohort of 431 patients, aspirin was associated with lower 2-year fellow-eye NAION (7% vs 15%) but little or no 5-year benefit.
title: Aspirin therapy in nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: Our results suggest a possible short-term but little or no long-term benefit to aspirin in reducing the risk of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy in the fellow eye.

claim: A retrospective study of 131 patients reported aspirin use was associated with reduced second-eye NAION (RR 0.44).
title: Aspirin reduces the incidence of second eye NAION: a retrospective study.
quote: Aspirin (65-1,300 mg) taken two or more times per week decreased the incidence (17.5% vs. 53.5%) and relative risk (RR = 0.44, p = 0.0002)

claim: A small retrospective series (n=52) reported less second-eye involvement with aspirin 325 mg/day (18%) than without aspirin (50%).
title: Role of aspirin in reducing the frequency of second eye involvement in patients with non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy.
quote: Second eye involvement was noted in 8 of 16 patients (50%) who did not receive aspirin

claim: In the prospective IONDT follow-up, aspirin use was not associated with new fellow-eye NAION.
title: The fellow eye in NAION: report from the ischemic optic neuropathy decompression trial follow-up study.
quote: but not age, sex, aspirin use, or smoking were significantly associated with new NAION in the fellow eye

claim: A 725-participant sham-controlled phase 2/3 trial of intravitreal QPI-1007 (caspase-2 siRNA) did not meet its primary endpoint, with benefit only in a low-acuity subgroup.
title: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Phase 2/3 Trial of QPI-1007 for Acute Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy.
quote: Although the primary outcome measure was not met, significant effects on preserving vision were observed in the subgroup of participants with baseline BCVA of 20/63 or worse.

claim: A 22-participant phase 2a trial of RPh201 in previous NAION showed no safety concerns and nonsignificant visual acuity differences.
title: Randomized Controlled Phase 2a Study of RPh201 in Previous Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy.
quote: No proven treatment exists for nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), either in the acute or late phase.

claim: A nonrandomized retrospective study of 37 patients suggested levodopa within 45 days of onset was associated with better acuity outcomes, without visual field difference.
title: Levodopa may improve vision loss in recent-onset, nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
quote: Patients treated with levodopa within 45 days of onset of NAION were more likely to experience improvement

claim: A 20-patient pilot RCT in chronic NAION reported a modest visual acuity gain with levodopa/carbidopa, pending confirmation in larger studies.
title: Effect of levodopa and carbidopa on recovery of visual function in patients with nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy of longer than six months' duration.
quote: Confirmation of our results is awaited from larger population studies

claim: GLP-1 is a 30-amino-acid peptide from intestinal L-cells that stimulates insulin and inhibits glucagon secretion, and is rapidly inactivated by dipeptidyl peptidase IV.
title: The physiology of glucagon-like peptide 1.
quote: GLP-1 is extremely rapidly metabolized and inactivated by the enzyme dipeptidyl peptidase IV even before the hormone has left the gut

claim: GLP-1 also slows gastrointestinal motility (the 'ileal brake') and appears to regulate appetite and food intake.
title: The physiology of glucagon-like peptide 1.
quote: It also inhibits gastrointestinal motility and secretion and thus acts as an enterogastrone and part of the "ileal brake" mechanism.

claim: The incretin effect, mediated by GIP and GLP-1, is defective in type 2 diabetes, in which the pancreas remains responsive to GLP-1 but not GIP.
title: The incretin effect in healthy individuals and those with type 2 diabetes: physiology, pathophysiology, and response to therapeutic interventions.
quote: In type 2 diabetes, the endocrine pancreas remains responsive to GLP-1 but is no longer responsive to GIP

claim: GLP-1 controls meal-related glycemia via insulin augmentation and glucagon inhibition and also inhibits gastric emptying and food intake, with GLP-1R-positive cell types mediating metabolic and non-glycemic actions.
title: Mechanisms of Action and Therapeutic Application of Glucagon-like Peptide-1.
quote: GLP-1 also inhibits gastric emptying and food intake, actions maximizing nutrient absorption while limiting weight gain.

claim: Native GLP-1 is degraded within about 2-3 minutes, and GLP-1RAs are classed as short-acting (exenatide, lixisenatide) or long-acting (liraglutide, dulaglutide, exenatide LAR) with different pharmacodynamic profiles.
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for individualized treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
quote: Native GLP-1 is degraded within ~2-3 min in the circulation

claim: GLP-1RAs are injected twice daily (exenatide), once daily (lixisenatide, liraglutide) or once weekly (exenatide QW, dulaglutide, semaglutide), and an oral daily semaglutide is also approved.
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists in the treatment of type 2 diabetes - state-of-the-art.
quote: At present, GLP-1 RAs are injected twice daily (exenatide b.i.d.), once daily (lixisenatide and liraglutide), or once weekly

claim: Long-acting GLP-1RAs have greater effects on fasting glucose and HbA1c, whereas effects on gastric emptying decrease over time (tachyphylaxis).
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists in the treatment of type 2 diabetes - state-of-the-art.
quote: Effects on gastric emptying decrease over time (tachyphylaxis).

claim: Semaglutide has an extended half-life of approximately 1 week.
title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
quote: semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide 1 analogue with an extended half-life of approximately 1 week

claim: In SUSTAIN-6 (n=3297), semaglutide reduced MACE (HR 0.74) but increased diabetic retinopathy complications (HR 1.76).
title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
quote: rates of retinopathy complications (vitreous hemorrhage, blindness, or conditions requiring treatment with an intravitreal agent or photocoagulation) were significantly higher (hazard ratio, 1.76

claim: In LEADER (n=9340), liraglutide reduced the primary MACE outcome (HR 0.87) and cardiovascular death (HR 0.78) versus placebo.
title: Liraglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes.
quote: hazard ratio, 0.87; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 0.97; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.01 for superiority

claim: In REWIND (n=9901), weekly dulaglutide 1.5 mg reduced MACE (HR 0.88) over a median 5.4 years.
title: Dulaglutide and cardiovascular outcomes in type 2 diabetes (REWIND): a double-blind, randomised placebo-controlled trial.

claim: In PIONEER 6 (n=3183), oral semaglutide was noninferior to placebo for MACE (HR 0.79).
title: Oral Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
quote: (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.57 to 1.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority)

claim: A meta-analysis of seven cardiovascular outcome trials (56,004 participants) found GLP-1RAs reduced MACE by 12% and all-cause mortality by 12%.
title: Cardiovascular, mortality, and kidney outcomes with GLP-1 receptor agonists in patients with type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cardiovascular outcome trials.
quote: Overall, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment reduced MACE by 12% (HR 0·88, 95% CI 0·82-0·94; p<0·0001).

claim: In SELECT (n=17,604), semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly reduced MACE (HR 0.80) in people with cardiovascular disease and overweight/obesity without diabetes.
title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity without Diabetes.
quote: (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% confidence interval, 0.72 to 0.90; P<0.001)

claim: In FLOW (n=3533), semaglutide 1.0 mg reduced major kidney disease events by 24% in type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease.
title: Effects of Semaglutide on Chronic Kidney Disease in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
quote: hazard ratio, 0.76; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 0.88; P = 0.0003

claim: In STEP 1, semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly produced a mean 14.9% weight reduction at 68 weeks versus 2.4% with placebo, with gastrointestinal events most common.
title: Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity.
quote: The mean change in body weight from baseline to week 68 was -14.9% in the semaglutide group as compared with -2.4% with placebo

claim: Tirzepatide, a dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist, produced 15.0-20.9% mean weight reduction at 72 weeks in SURMOUNT-1, with GI adverse events mainly during dose escalation.
title: Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity.
quote: The most common adverse events with tirzepatide were gastrointestinal, and most were mild to moderate in severity, occurring primarily during dose escalation.

claim: In SURPASS-2, tirzepatide lowered HbA1c by 2.01-2.30 percentage points versus 1.86 with semaglutide 1 mg over 40 weeks.
title: Tirzepatide versus Semaglutide Once Weekly in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
quote: -2.01 percentage points, -2.24 percentage points, and -2.30 percentage points with 5 mg, 10 mg, and 15 mg of tirzepatide

claim: A network meta-analysis of 60 trials found GLP-1RAs modestly reduced systolic blood pressure and slightly increased heart rate.
